newsitem.title: ITALY: Flights cancelled as Rome air controllers strike.
newsitem.headline: Flights cancelled as Rome air controllers strike.

text.p: Air traffic controllers staged a four-hour strike on Tuesday at Rome's main Fiumicino airport, causing delays to services and the cancellation of numerous flights, airport officials said.
State flag-carrier Alitalia said it had to cancel 66 international and domestic flights, while British Airways, Lufthansa and Air France were also forced to abandon services.
Unions called the air traffic controllers' strike to demand guarantees for the future of the national flight control body.
Further delays were expected on Wednesday when air traffic controllers at Rome's second airport, Ciampino, are due to hold their own four hour stoppage between noon and 4 p.m. (1100-1500 GMT).
